name: Massage Therapist
seoTitle: Business Insurance Cost for Massage Therapists

industryContext.contextNote: Massage therapists provide hands-on bodywork in close physical contact with clients, creating bodily-injury and misconduct-allegation exposure unique to touch-based services.

riskFactors.title: Injury During Treatment
riskFactors.description: Deep tissue or therapeutic techniques applied incorrectly can aggravate an existing injury or cause new soreness and bruising, leading to claims.

riskFactors.title: Pre-Existing Condition Aggravation
riskFactors.description: Clients with undisclosed medical conditions can experience adverse reactions to massage techniques, creating liability exposure.

riskFactors.title: Premises & Equipment Liability
riskFactors.description: Massage tables, hot stone equipment, and treatment room hazards can cause slip-and-fall or equipment-related injuries.

faqs.question: Why do massage therapists need Professional Liability insurance?
faqs.answer: Professional Liability covers claims that a specific technique or treatment caused injury or aggravated a condition, which General Liability does not cover.

faqs.question: What is the average cost of business insurance for a massage therapist?
faqs.answer: A massage therapist in the $0-50k revenue tier pays an estimated $285 per year for baseline General Liability coverage.

faqs.question: Do mobile massage therapists need different coverage?
faqs.answer: Mobile therapists who travel to client homes often need to confirm their policy covers off-premises work, and may need Commercial Auto if using a vehicle for business travel.

faqs.question: Does massage therapist insurance require a license?
faqs.answer: Most carriers require an active state massage therapy license to issue Professional Liability coverage, since the policy is underwritten around licensed scope of practice.

blogContent.whyThisRiskFactor: Massage therapists carry a 1.2 actuarial risk factor, reflecting hands-on physical contact and treatment-related injury exposure.
blogContent.howCalculated: Premiums scale with revenue tier, staff count, and Professional Liability endorsements covering treatment-related claims.
blogContent.comparisonNote: Massage therapist premiums are comparable to dog groomers and real estate agents, and slightly below other personal-care professions like estheticians.
